identity_chain: Equinix's OS1 facility page, read through the Internet Archive's raw copy of 3 October 2026 (ia-eqx-os1-20261003.html, sha256 74b29529...b2798b3b), names 'Osaka OS1' and gives its address as '1-26-1, Shinmachi, Nishi-ku / Nishi Shinsaibashi Building / Osaka, 550 0013 / Japan', with 6,015 m2 (64,745 ft2) of colocation space in an 11-storey steel-frame building.
GSI's address search for 大阪府大阪市西区新町1-26-1 returns exactly one feature, titled 大阪府大阪市西区新町一丁目２６番１号, at 135.495911, 34.675838 (house-number level).
GSI's reverse geocoder returns municipality code 27106 (Osaka City, Nishi-ku) and 新町一丁目 for that point (gsi-revgeo-osaka-os1.json).

On GSI's standard-map tile z17/114868/52061 the point falls at pixel (142.3, 33.7), on the eastern street line of a block whose main building is drawn with diagonal hatching and spans about 50 m east-west (pixels 88-139 at 0.98 m per pixel); the point is about 3-4 m east of that building's outline. On tile z18/229737/104122 the point (pixel 28.5, 67.3) lies on the block line about 2.5 m east of the building outline (0.49 m per pixel).

Equinix's own page markup carries a map-centre attribute for the page's location widget (135.49586917748803, 34.67556233755475); it is 30.8 m south of the GSI point (pyproj WGS84 geodesic), inside the same block. It is noted only as a cross-check and is not the locator.
extent_review: Equinix publishes no building outline. The building drawn at the point spans about 50 m east-west and about 35 m north-south on GSI's z17 standard map, so the data-centre floor space lies within roughly 60 m of the point.
not_used: No Google, Apple, Bing, HERE, Waze or other commercial web map, PeeringDB or OpenStreetMap data was opened or used.
The Equinix page's map-centre attribute (display widget) was not used as the locator; it is reported only as a 30.8 m cross-check.
uncertainty_reason: GSI publishes no positional accuracy for house-number address points; the point sits on the street frontage at the eastern edge of the address building, which extends about 50 m west and 35 m north-south, so the data-centre space may lie up to about 60 m from the point.
tools: Tile pixel positions and distances computed with Python (pyproj 3.7.1 for geodesics); tiles viewed for identity review only, not for status.
